opex.name: Research and development, net
opex.note: Developing the Neutron rocket, Electron and spacecraft — up 25% from $66M a year earlier.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Running and selling the company — up 50% from $40M a year earlier, including deal costs for acquisitions.

footerNote: Net loss is the filed $49.3M; the loss per share attributable to common stockholders was -$0.08.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue was a record $234M, up from $144M in Q2 2025

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP, diluted)
kpis.note: Basic and diluted; net loss was $49M, vs -$0.13 and a $66M loss a year earlier

kpis.label: Backlog
kpis.note: Orders booked but not yet flown or built; up 137% year over year — $1.42B Space Systems and $940M Launch Services

kpis.label: Cash
kpis.note: Cash and equivalents at June 30, plus $258M in marketable securities

oneTimers: $8.6M of transaction costs sit inside SG&A in Q2 (per the non-GAAP reconciliation in the release) — deal costs tied to closing the Mynaric and Motiv acquisitions and the announced Iridium deal. They are part of the reported $49M loss, not on top of it.
otherDetail: Other income was $13.6M net: $16.5M of interest income on the large cash pile, partly offset by a $2.0M foreign-exchange loss, $0.6M of interest expense and $0.4M of other expense.

segments.name: Launch Services
segments.note: Rockets: Electron and HASTE launches. Six Electron missions flew in the quarter, but sales dipped on the timing of when launch revenue is recognised.

segments.name: Space Systems
segments.note: Satellites, spacecraft parts and mission services — now about four-fifths of all sales, boosted by large government satellite work.

takeaways.text: Space Systems revenue nearly doubled to $189M and is now 81% of sales. Launch Services slipped 4% to $45M even though six Electron missions flew, because two were HASTE missions whose revenue had partly been recognised in earlier quarters.
takeaways.title: Growth came from satellites, not just rockets

takeaways.text: Backlog — orders booked but not yet flown or built — hit $2.36B, up 137% year over year, with about 45% expected to turn into revenue within 12 months. Rocket Lab guided Q3 revenue to $250M–$265M, another record if it lands.
takeaways.title: Backlog is at a record — and Q3 is guided higher

takeaways.text: Gross profit jumped to $85M, yet $82M of research and development plus $60M of SG&A left a $58M operating loss. The $49M net loss was smaller than the $66M loss a year earlier, and a $2.13B cash balance gives the company room to keep funding Neutron, whose first Stage 1 tank is targeted for delivery to the launch pad in Q4 2026.
takeaways.title: Still losing money, but the loss narrowed

verdict: Rocket Lab grew revenue 62% to a record $234M and lifted its backlog to a record $2.36B, but it still lost $49M as research and overhead outran its gross profit.
